content.title: About
content.content: Cooked cabbage is a leafy vegetable obtained by heat‑treating head cabbage. The cooking process retains most of its vitamins and minerals while softening the texture, making it easy to eat and versatile in cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cabbage belongs to the Brassicaceae family and is a relative of broccoli, cauliflower, and Brussels sprouts.
Archaeological evidence suggests cabbage was domesticated in Eastern Europe over 4,000 years ago.
Cooked cabbage is a staple in many traditional dishes: bigos (Poland), sauerkraut (Germany), cabbage noodle soup (China).
It contains glucosinolates, which break down into isothiocyanates with potential anti‑cancer properties.
When stored properly, cooked cabbage can last in the refrigerator for up to 5 days.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Cooked cabbage retains a good amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Contains potassium and magnesium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure, while magnesium is important for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Cooked cabbage is low in calories, making it a great choice for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Cabbage contains raffinose, which can cause gas in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Interaction with blood thinners
items.content: High vitamin K content may reduce the effectiveness of anticoagulant medications.

items.title: Loss of some vitamins with prolonged cooking
items.content: Extended heat exposure can diminish vitamin C and certain folates.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked cabbage can be served as a side dish, added to soups, stews, salads, or used as a filling for pies and pancakes. It pairs well with meat, fish, and legumes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked cabbage in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. It stays fresh for up to 5 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
